I'm thinking about switching this to use patch instead of update in this PR. StrategicMergePatch is used by kubelet to add conditions, and it seems to work ok. It will also mean smaller payloads. WDYT @atiratree @liggitt @apelisse @alculquicondor ?

EDIT: I pushed a commit to use Patch instead. PTAL. It means smaller payloads when adding the condition and setting the phase. The field manager for the modified fields is recorded as `kube-controller-manager`, not `PodGC`. I think doing of the fields is probably ok, which is what would happen using SSA patch before.
For the update to work I had to also add the update role. It's not relevant change if we go with patch, but might be good to do anyway.
/retest

> I'm thinking about switching this to use patch instead of update in this PR. StrategicMergePatch is used by kubelet to add conditions, and it seems to work ok. It will also mean smaller payloads. WDYT @atiratree @liggitt @apelisse @alculquicondor ?

Thanks for the fix. I was able to test and make sure that the changes help with fixing the bug and the GC is able to clean up the pods.

@alculquicondor @liggitt i only see one use of `PodConditionApplyConfiguration` that's already in this PR:
https://cs.k8s.io/?q=PodConditionApplyConfiguration&i=nope&files=&excludeFiles=_test%5C.go&repos=kubernetes/kubernetes

@dims I think these are the other places:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6d70013af571e389d19fb390eb7cb89dca41ae81/pkg/controller/disruption/disruption.go#L776-L782

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6d70013af571e389d19fb390eb7cb89dca41ae81/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/scheduler/taint_manager.go#L131-L138

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6d70013af571e389d19fb390eb7cb89dca41ae81/pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/preemption.go#L366-L374

gotcha now i now what to look for! [grep.txt](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/files/12974099/grep.txt) shows the same spots using `rg --multiline --multiline-dotall "DisruptionTarget\).*ApplyStatus\("`

In the last commit I move the other remaining places to SMP. PTAL. Two remarks:
1. First, no integration tests reproducing the issue for the other places. Seems enough to demonstrate the issue in one place (podgc).

2. In disruption.go we used to pass resource version. We didn't have any tests showing this is really needed and it does not seem needed. The potential race condition is when disruption controller decides to change the Status to False (after 2 min). Then, another controller in between Get by the disruption controller re-adds the condition with `Status=True` and new `LastTransitionTime`. As a result the pod might get deleted when the `DisruptionTarget` `Status=False` (just after being flipped by disruption.go). This scenario seems very unlikely, and with limited consequences. Let me know if we care, and in case we care there does not seem to be a way to pass resource version in PatchPodStatus, so probably I would need to use Update in this case. WDYT @liggitt @alculquicondor ?

/lgtm

/assign @liggitt @alculquicondor

issue_context.title: Pod Garbage collector fails to clean up  PODs from nodes that are not running anymore
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

This happened after upgrading to Kubernetes 1.26 from 1.24

The succession of events we have observed:
- Our workloads use HorizontalPodAutoscaler to scale up due to traffic increase
- Cluster Autoscaler provisions new nodes to accommodate the new replicas
- Traffic goes down
- HPA downsize replicas
- Cluster Autoscaler notices nodes under the threshold of usage and PODs can be accommodated into other nodes
- Nodes are drained and downscaled
- Kubernetes still reports PODs in a "Running" or "Terminating" state in the node that no longer exists
- Kubernetes control plane reports "Orphan pods" on its audit logs

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubernetes Garbage collector to clean up these PODs after the node is gone

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Deploy the following yaml deployments into a K8s cluster 1.26 and terminate one of the nodes

(duplicated port key "containerPort + protocol")
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nginx
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: nginx
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: nginx
    app.kubernetes.io/component: deployment
spec:
  replicas: 100
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: nginx
      app.kubernetes.io/instance: nginx
      app.kubernetes.io/component: deployment
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: nginx
        app.kubernetes.io/instance: nginx
        app.kubernetes.io/component: deployment
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Always
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: "nginx:latest"
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: http
              protocol: TCP
            - containerPort: 8080
              name: metrics
              protocol: TCP
```

```
from typing import List

from kubernetes import client, config
from kubernetes.client.models import V1NodeList, V1Pod, V1PodList
from kubernetes.client.rest import ApiException
from loguru import logger


def get_core_v1_api() -> client.CoreV1Api:
    config.load_incluster_config()
    return client.CoreV1Api()


def get_orphan_pods(v1_client: client.CoreV1Api) -> List[V1Pod]:
    """
    Pods that seem to be running in nodes that don't exist anymore
    """
    nodes: V1NodeList = v1_client.list_node(watch=False)
    all_node_names = [no.metadata.name for no in nodes.items]
    logger.info(f"Nodes found: {all_node_names}")
    pods: V1PodList = v1_client.list_pod_for_all_namespaces(watch=False)
    return [po for po in pods.items if po.spec.node_name not in all_node_names]


def kill_pods(v1_client: client.CoreV1Api, pods: List[V1Pod]) -> None:
    logger.info(f"Orphan PODs found: {len(pods)}")
    for pod_to_kill in pods:
        # Create an instance of the API class
        name = pod_to_kill.metadata.name
        namespace = pod_to_kill.metadata.namespace

        logger.info(f"Killing {namespace}/{name}")
        try:
            v1_client.delete_namespaced_pod(name, namespace, grace_period_seconds=0)
            logger.info(f"Killed {namespace}/{name}")
        except ApiException as k8s_exception:
            logger.warning(
                f"Exception when calling CoreV1Api->delete_namespaced_pod: {k8s_exception}",
            )
```

Why isn't this using SMP patch (`PatchPodStatus`) like the other places?

Doing an update like this with no resourceVersion set in UpdateOptions can stomp other pod status changes made by other clients. Adding a resourceVersion precondition would unnecessarily encounter conflict errors if unrelated changes were made by other clients.

The intention of using update here is to fail on conflicts. I describe the possible scenario here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121103#pullrequestreview-1685540049.

Basically, if we don't check resource  version here, it is possible (but unlikely) the pod will be deleted when `DisruptionTarget=False`, if the disruption controller switches the status from True to False due to categorizing it as stale after 2min, and in this time another controller updates the condition (with new LastTransitionTime).

As for achieving the failing on resource version, we use [UpdateStatus in Job](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/145b84b0b17e5f8e07697f455c6646406bc92149/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L1678) without passing it explicitly and it fails on conflicts. Because it is rare, and negative path (the other controlled to succeed with Patch, but fail with Delete), I think correctness might be more important than performance. Still, I'm ok with both approaches, just outlining the reasoning.
